attributableVsGroupProfit.title: Attributable net income vs consolidated group profit
attributableVsGroupProfit.content:
Net income is profit attributable to PCCW's own shareholders after deducting the share that belongs to non-controlling interests (NCI) and perpetual capital securities. Profit for the period is the full consolidated result -- 100% of HKT's and Viu's profit -- before that deduction.

For PCCW Limited: PCCW owns roughly 52% of HKT but consolidates all of it, so most of consolidated profit (~HK$2.6bn in FY2025 against a headline HK$2,615m group profit) never reaches PCCW's own equity holders. That NCI claim, plus distributions on PCCW's perpetual capital securities, is why PCCW has posted an attributable net loss (-HK$253m FY2025, -HK$300m FY2024) every year this chart covers even as the group business is solidly profitable and growing.

What to watch:

  • Whether the gap between the two bars is widening or narrowing -- it tracks HKT's profit growth and PCCW's effective ownership stake, not PCCW's own operations
  • Any change in PCCW's stake in HKT (further sell-downs would widen the gap further)
  • The DCF values PCCW off its own owner FCF and equity claim, not the consolidated total

attributableVsGroupEquity.title: Attributable equity vs total equity including NCI
attributableVsGroupEquity.content:
Shareholders' equity is PCCW's own book value: assets less liabilities less the non-controlling interests' share. Total equity including NCI adds back that minority share -- mostly outside investors' ~48% claim on HKT.

For PCCW Limited: cumulative losses, dividends paid up from HKT (a chunk of which is passed straight through to HKT's own minority holders) and PCCW's perpetual capital securities have driven PCCW's own attributable equity negative since FY2025 (-HK$1,966m at FY2025, -HK$4,207m at H1 FY2026), even though group equity including NCI is still positive. A negative book value at the parent level does not mean HKT itself is impaired -- it reflects how the holding-company structure and capital returns are funded.

What to watch:

  • Whether the NCI share of equity is shrinking (would narrow the gap) or PCCW's own equity keeps deteriorating
  • Dividend and distribution policy relative to attributable earnings, since PCCW cannot sustain payouts from a shrinking equity base indefinitely

capexSplit.title: CapEx split: network/PP&E vs intangibles
capexSplit.content:
PP&E capex is spending on physical network infrastructure and equipment; intangibles capex covers spectrum licences, software and other non-physical assets.

For PCCW Limited: intangibles capex has consistently run larger than PP&E capex at HKT (e.g. HK$5,598m vs HK$2,068m in FY2025) and has grown faster over the last several years, reflecting spectrum renewals and software/platform investment alongside a more disciplined physical network build. FY-only, since the interim filings do not split CapEx this way.

What to watch:

  • Step-changes in intangibles capex around spectrum auction/renewal years
  • Whether total CapEx (the two bars stacked) is growing faster than EBITDA, which would erode owner FCF

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For PCCW Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For PCCW Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For PCCW Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For PCCW Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For PCCW Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For PCCW Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For PCCW Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For PCCW Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For PCCW Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For PCCW Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
